title: Finite initial storage limits the onset signal between recharge loss and stream diversion in parallel linear stores
abstract: We test how the onset of a permanent runoff loss can separate reduced recharge from stream diversion. In fixed parallel linear stores with unchanged initial states and uniform gains, all later forced responses depend only on the product of the two gains. Only initial-state drainage separates them. We prove a sharp flow-gap bound of (1-f)S/(e t) and a sharp remaining signal-energy bound of (1-f)^2 S^2/(4 e d), for initial connected storage S, common final gain f and observation delay d. The bounds cover any positive store mixture and any later recharge history. In an ideal Gaussian observation model they give a sharp ceiling on correct attribution from the entire later record. A synthetic case with S=120 mm and f=0.784 has a largest one-year flow gap of 0.02612 mm/day. Independent state integration, high-precision convolution, exact sharpness cases and 5,000 random mixtures check the code. Initial-state reset gives exact ambiguity, and nonuniform routing defeats the scalar sign test. This is a method and synthetic study, not an Australian field estimate. Effective recharge, a known change date, initial storage, counterfactual flow and the observation-error model limit field use.

display.caption: Synthetic onset responses, sharp storage bounds and an ideal observation limit. No field data are shown.
